correctness.rationale: Derive all vertices from the strict facet inequalities and prove they are distinct. For a uniform nonempty subset and symmetric sign, count one- and two-coordinate events exactly and obtain Σ_ii and Σ_ij. Constant diagonal/off-diagonal form implies transverse and axial eigenvalues; the ratio simplifies to 1 + d/2^d ((2^d-1)x²+2x-1), with x=a/(ℓ-a). The derivative is strictly positive on x>0 and endpoint ratio 1-d/2^d is positive; the unique root x=1/(2^(d/2)+1) gives the claimed unique isotropy, strict eigenvalue ordering and condition-number minimum. Radius differences equal a(ℓ-a)>0, so the tight frame is noncospherical. A standalone exact-rational checker passed on 35 dimension/cant profiles (5,010 vertices processed), with six exact even-dimensional roots and five high-precision odd-dimensional checks; these finite tests supplement, not replace, the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2020 primary identifies these polytopes and their vertex combinatorics, not their uniform-vertex covariance. The 2024 and 2025 continuations treat volume, facets, face volumes, tiling, and symmetries. Full primary text for the 2020 and 2025 sources and full text of both closest same-object mathematical findings were compared by mathematical implication: known radial shells constrain only diagonal traces, and optimal John/Löwner ellipsoids concern extremal volume rather than the equally weighted vertex moment matrix. A separate prior uniform-VOLUME covariance result uses a different measure (and different extremal cant). No identified source states or implies the vertex-uniform covariance eigenvalues and unique isotropy ratio without additional moment calculation. This is a best-knowledge priority assessment, not a proof of uniqueness in the literature.

value.rationale: The result is a complete natural classification of vertex-uniform inertia for an established cubical-zonotope family in every dimension and every strict cant, not a discretionary finite slice. The unique dimension-dependent isotropy ratio 1/(2+2^(d/2)) gives an exact tight-frame realization that is nevertheless noncospherical, and identifies the global best covariance conditioning and eigenspace reversal. The exact invariant can be used to compare canonical polytope embeddings and to distinguish discrete vertex isotropy from continuous-volume isotropy and Löwner/John optimal ellipsoids. No speculative downstream theorem is needed to support this self-contained value.
